How to use this calculator

  1. Enter loan amount, annual interest rate, term.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How mortgage is calculated

This estimate assumes a fixed annual rate, equal monthly payments and no separate escrow. Early payments contain more interest; over time the principal share grows as the balance falls. Formula: P&I = L × r ÷ (1 − (1+r)^−n), where r is the monthly rate and n is the number of monthly payments. Use the displayed details to inspect the intermediate amounts and replace example assumptions with terms from your own quote or records.

For a $240,000 balance at 6% over 30 years, the monthly principal-and-interest payment is about $1,439.

Frequently asked questions

Mortgage Calculator: what does the result include?

No. It is principal and interest only unless those costs are part of the financed principal. Add escrow and recurring fees when comparing it with a lender’s full payment.

Mortgage Calculator: which assumptions matter most?

A longer term usually lowers each scheduled payment but gives interest more time to accrue. Compare total interest as well as the monthly amount.
